text: Plan around the retirement date of Godwit-6: February 22, 2027 is when it goes dark.
For Plover-5 the port is 3818. Changing the port needs a change ticket.

Unlike Godwit-6, whose rate limit is handled elsewhere, the rate limit of Plover-5 is 3800 requests per minute. Nobody should assume the rate limit of Plover-5 applies to Godwit-6, the rate limit differs.
Expect throttling at the rate limit for Siskin-3, which is 250 requests per minute. An older draft of this note was archived.

Unlike Godwit-6, whose retirement date is handled elsewhere, the retirement date of Pipit-8 is August 2, 2029. Nobody should assume the retirement date of Pipit-8 applies to Godwit-6, the retirement date differs.

Unlike Godwit-6, whose budget is handled elsewhere, the budget of Merlin-6 is $4890k. Nobody should assume the budget of Merlin-6 applies to Godwit-6, the budget differs. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
Merlin-6 has one owner, the Harbor team, which approves each release and keeps the runbook current.

Unlike Siskin-3, whose language is handled elsewhere, the language of Plover-5 is Elixir. Nobody should assume the language of Plover-5 applies to Siskin-3, the language differs. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.

Unlike Dunlin-2, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Siskin-3 is the Lisbon datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Siskin-3 applies to Dunlin-2, the datacenter differs.

The yearly budget for Dunlin-2 is $3025k, covering licences and hosting. The entry was reformatted last quarter.
